summary: Okanogan National Forest summit lookout built 1933 on a pole L-4 tower; sold and removed in 1951; no lookout stands on the summit, reached by a 10-mile hike on an abandoned trail.

facts.design: Pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Sold and removed in 1951. No lookout stands on the summit, per a 2022 visit.

access.note: Okanogan National Forest land, reached from the Wolf Creek Trailhead; no closure or permit is described in these sources; the site is isolated from any maintained trail

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists a 10-mile one-way hiking distance, and its directions end at the Wolf Creek Trailhead; the final route follows an abandoned trail that has faded in places

events.note: George Haase, fireman-lookout; fire season started July 15, 1932
Register gives 1933 for an 18-foot pole L-4 tower; newspaper and WillhiteWeb place construction in 1933
Sold for $1.00 and removed; the register says the tower was sold, WillhiteWeb says the cab
Registered November 18, 2012 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1932 newspaper items describe plans for a cabin and lookout houses, and WillhiteWeb says the L-4 cab and pole tower materials were packed up that fall; the September 1933 newspaper item and WillhiteWeb describe construction that year, which matches the register's 1933 build date

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: 18 feet in the register and on firelookout.com, 20 feet in the 1933 Wenatchee item. The record's height_m of 6.1 (20 ft) follows the newspaper. It was left unchanged and no height fact is published. Sold item: the register says the tower was sold, WillhiteWeb says the cab was; the story gives both. The staffing name is from the 1932 newspaper and WillhiteWeb; no other personal details are included. The WTA hike page loaded with no usable text. Used 1 WebSearch and 5 page reads.
